issues.description: SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() is specified in the UML as returning void, but the reference solution implements it as `public boolean checkOrderReady()`. Students following the UML signature will implement a void method, which would not match the reference solution/tests expecting the boolean signature (or vice versa).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the signature across all artifacts: either change the solution to `public void checkOrderReady()` (remove the boolean return value and related logic), or update the UML/spec to explicitly require `boolean checkOrderReady()`.

issues.description: The specification contradicts itself about SealSaloon.stock: it first describes it as an instance field (`final Stock stock` initialized in the constructor), but later explicitly requires the `stock` attribute to be static (shared across instances). The solution implements `private static final Stock stock`, making it unclear whether students should implement per-instance or shared stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Decide on one design and make all artifacts consistent: (a) shared stock: update wording/UML to `static final Stock stock`; or (b) per-instance stock: remove the static requirement and implement `private final Stock stock` initialized in the constructor.

issues.description: The UML lists only Stock methods add/take/findStockIngredient/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock, but both template and solution expose an additional public method `setStockIngredients(...)`. This extra public API conflicts with the stated focus on getters for private fields and can mislead students about the required interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove `setStockIngredients` from the public API (use only the UML-listed methods plus getters), or update the UML/spec to include `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])` if it is intended to be part of the required interface.

issues.description: The UML shows SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int) as instance methods, but the written specification later mandates both methods must be static. The solution implements both as static, so students relying on the UML may implement instance methods that do not match the intended API/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make UML/spec consistent with the intended static design: mark calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery as static in the UML (and ensure stock is also specified as static), or remove the static requirement and implement them as instance methods everywhere.
